records.source: וּכְכַלּ֣וֹת כָּל־זֹ֗את יָצְא֨וּ כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥להַֽנִּמְצְאִים֮ לְעָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָה֒ וַיְשַׁבְּר֣וּ הַמַּצֵּב֣וֹת וַיְגַדְּע֣וּ הָאֲשֵׁרִ֡ים וַיְנַתְּצ֣וּ אֶת־הַ֠בָּמוֹת וְאֶת־הַֽמִּזְבְּחֹ֞ת מִכָּל־יְהוּדָ֧ה וּבִנְיָמִ֛ן וּבְאֶפְרַ֥יִם וּמְנַשֶּׁ֖ה עַד־לְכַלֵּ֑ה וַיָּשׁ֜וּבוּ כָּל־בְּנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אִ֥ישׁ לַאֲחֻזָּת֖וֹ לְעָרֵיהֶֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And when finished all this, went out all Israel, the [ones] found, to [the] cities of Judah, and broke the standing stones, and cut down the Asherim, and tore down the high places and the altars from all Judah and Benjamin and in Ephraim and Manasseh, until finishing; and returned all [the] sons of Israel, each to his possession, to their cities.
pieces: When all this was over, all Israel who were there went out to the towns of Judah. They smashed the standing stones, cut down the Asherah poles, and tore down the high places and the altars throughout Judah and Benjamin, and in Ephraim and Manasseh as well, until they had destroyed them all. Then all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} went back to their own towns, each to his own property.

L.1: And when all this was finished, all Israel who were present went out to the cities of Judah, and they broke the standing stones and cut down the Asherah poles and tore down the high places and the altars out of all Judah and Benjamin, and in Ephraim and Manasseh, until [they had] finished. And all the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel returned, each to his possession, to their cities.

R.1: When the festival was over, all Israel who were there went out to the towns of Judah. They smashed the stone pillars and cut down the poles used to worship Asherah. They tore down the hilltop shrines and the altars all over Judah and Benjamin, and in Ephraim and Manasseh too, until they had destroyed every one. Then all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} went home to their own land and their own towns.

decisions.choice: when all this was finished: when the Passover and the festival that followed it were over
decisions.reason: "All this" points back to chapter 30: the Passover, the seven days of the Festival of Unleavened Bread, and the seven further days the assembly chose to keep (30:21-26). The cleansing of the land follows straight on from the festival.

decisions.choice: standing stones, Asherah poles, high places and altars: places and objects of worship outside the temple
decisions.reason: Standing stones were upright stones set up as sacred markers, and Asherah poles were wooden poles or images standing for the goddess Asherah; the law ordered both destroyed (Exodus 34:13; Deuteronomy 7:5; 12:3). The high places were local shrines, often on hills, where sacrifices were made away from the one place Yahweh chose (Deuteronomy 12:2-5).

decisions.choice: Judah and Benjamin, Ephraim and Manasseh: the cleansing reaches the old northern kingdom too
decisions.reason: Judah and Benjamin made up Hezekiah's kingdom; Ephraim and Manasseh were the heart of the northern kingdom, which Assyria had destroyed (2 Kings 17:6). Hezekiah had already invited the north to his Passover (30:1, 10-11, 18). 2 Kings 18:4 says that Hezekiah removed the high places and broke the standing stones; Chronicles tells how the people who had kept the festival carried this out across the whole land.

decisions.choice: until finishing: until everything was destroyed
decisions.reason: The same verb that opens the verse ("when all this was finished") closes the work: they did not stop until the task was complete.

decisions.choice: stone pillars, poles used to worship Asherah, hilltop shrines
decisions.reason: The wording kept for these words in Samuel, Kings and Chronicles, as 2 Kings 18:4.

decisions.choice: When the festival was over
decisions.reason: Readable names what "all this" refers to: the Passover festival of chapter 30.

records.heading: Contributions for the priests and Levites

records.source: וַיַּעֲמֵ֣ד יְחִזְקִיָּ֡הוּ אֶת־מַחְלְק֣וֹת הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים וְ֠הַלְוִיִּם עַֽל־מַחְלְקוֹתָ֞ם אִ֣ישׁ׀כְּפִ֣י עֲבֹדָת֗וֹ לַכֹּהֲנִים֙ וְלַלְוִיִּ֔ם לְעֹלָ֖ה וְלִשְׁלָמִ֑ים לְשָׁרֵת֙ וּלְהֹד֣וֹת וּלְהַלֵּ֔ל בְּשַׁעֲרֵ֖י מַחֲנ֥וֹת יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And appointed Hezekiah the divisions of the priests and the Levites by their divisions, each according to [the] mouth of his service, for the priests and for the Levites, for burnt offering and for peace offerings, to minister and to give thanks and to praise in [the] gates of [the] camps of Yahweh.
pieces: Hezekiah set the priests and the Levites in their divisions, each man according to his service, both priests and Levites, for burnt offerings and peace offerings, to minister and to give thanks and praise in the gates of the camps of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.2: And Hezekiah appointed the divisions of the priests and the Levites by their divisions, each according to his service, the priests and the Levites, for burnt offering and for peace offerings, to minister and to give thanks and to praise in the gates of the camps of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.2: Hezekiah organized the priests and the Levites into their groups, and gave each man his own work. They were in charge of the burnt offerings and the peace offerings. They also served, gave thanks and praised God at the gates of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple.

decisions.choice: divisions: the groups that took turns serving at the temple
decisions.reason: David had arranged the priests in twenty-four divisions and the Levites in groups, each serving in its turn (1 Chronicles 23-26). Hezekiah puts that order back in place after the temple had been shut under Ahaz (28:24; 29:3).

decisions.choice: the duties listed belong to both groups together
decisions.reason: The verse names the priests and the Levites and then their work as one list. The priests offered the burnt offerings and peace offerings, and the Levites helped them and led the thanksgiving and praise (1 Chronicles 23:28-31), but the verse does not split the list between them.

decisions.choice: the gates of the camps of Yahweh: the gates of the temple
alternatives: the gates of the temple courts
the gates of the Levites' quarters
decisions.reason: The temple is spoken of as Yahweh's camp, recalling the camp of Israel in the wilderness, with the tabernacle at its center and the Levites camped around it (Numbers 2-3). 1 Chronicles 9:18-19 uses the same picture for the gatekeepers. The exact sense of the plural "camps" is not certain: it may mean the temple courts, or the whole area where the priests and Levites served.

decisions.choice: praised God at the gates of the LORD's temple
decisions.reason: Readable supplies the object of the praise, and says "temple" for the picture of Yahweh's camps, as the meaning decision explains. Literal and Balanced keep "the camps of the LORD".

decisions.choice: They were in charge of the burnt offerings and the peace offerings. They also served ...
decisions.reason: Readable splits the purposes into short sentences.

records.source: וּמְנָת֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ מִן־רְכוּשׁ֜וֹ לָעֹל֗וֹת לְעֹלוֹת֙ הַבֹּ֣קֶר וְהָעֶ֔רֶב וְהָ֣עֹל֔וֹת לַשַּׁבָּת֖וֹת וְלֶחֳדָשִׁ֣ים וְלַמֹּעֲדִ֑ים כַּכָּת֖וּב בְּתוֹרַ֥ת יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And [the] portion of the king from his property [was] for the burnt offerings: for [the] burnt offerings of the morning and the evening, and the burnt offerings for the sabbaths and for the new moons and for the appointed feasts, as [it is] written in [the] law of Yahweh.
pieces: The king's share from his own possessions went for the burnt offerings: those offered morning and evening, and those for the Sabbaths, the new moons and the appointed festivals, as it is written in the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.3: And the portion of the king from his property [was] for the burnt offerings: for the burnt offerings of the morning and the evening, and the burnt offerings for the Sabbaths and for the new moons and for the appointed feasts, as [it is] written in the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.3: The king gave from what he himself owned for the burnt offerings. These were the burnt offerings each morning and evening, and those on Sabbath days, at new moon festivals and at the other set festivals, as the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says.

decisions.choice: the king's portion from his property: what the king himself gave from his own goods and herds
decisions.reason: The word for property covers movable wealth, including livestock (Genesis 13:6; 2 Chronicles 32:29). The king pays for the regular public offerings from his own wealth, as David and Solomon had done (1 Chronicles 29:3; 2 Chronicles 8:12-13).

decisions.choice: as written in the law: the offerings set out in Numbers 28-29
decisions.reason: The law fixes a burnt offering every morning and evening (Numbers 28:3-8), extra offerings on each Sabbath (28:9-10), at each new moon (28:11-15), and at the appointed festivals (28:16-29:39).

decisions.choice: the other set festivals
decisions.reason: Readable says "other" because the Sabbaths and new moons are also set times; the appointed festivals are the yearly ones.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָעָם֙ לְיוֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם לָתֵ֕ת מְנָ֥ת הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֑ם לְמַ֥עַן יֶחֶזְק֖וּ בְּתוֹרַ֥ת יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he said to the people, to [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem, to give [the] portion of the priests and the Levites, so that they may be strong in [the] law of Yahweh.
pieces: He also told the people who lived in Jerusalem to give the priests and the Levites their share, so that they could give themselves fully to the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.4: And he said to the people, to those living in Jerusalem, to give the portion of the priests and the Levites, so that they might be strong in the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.4: He ordered the people living in Jerusalem to give the priests and the Levites the share that belonged to them. Then they would be free to give all their time to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s law.

decisions.choice: be strong in the law of Yahweh: give themselves fully to the law
decisions.reason: "Be strong" here means to hold firmly and give one's strength to something. With their food supplied, the priests and Levites could keep to their work of serving and teaching the law (17:8-9; Deuteronomy 33:10) instead of leaving it to work their own fields, as later happened when the portions were not given (Nehemiah 13:10).

decisions.choice: the portion of the priests and the Levites: the share the law assigns them
decisions.reason: The priests and Levites had no tribal land; the law gave them parts of the offerings, the firstfruits and the tithes instead (Numbers 18:8-32; Deuteronomy 18:1-5).

decisions.choice: said ... to give: ordered them to give
decisions.reason: "Said" followed by "to give" is a command from the king.

decisions.choice: give themselves fully to
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the idiom "be strong in" into plain English; Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: Then they would be free to give all their time to
decisions.reason: Readable says what the share made possible: the priests and Levites did not have to support themselves in other ways.

records.source: וְכִפְרֹ֣ץ הַדָּבָ֗ר הִרְבּ֤וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ רֵאשִׁ֣ית דָּגָ֗ן תִּיר֤וֹשׁ וְיִצְהָר֙ וּדְבַ֔שׁ וְכֹ֖ל תְּבוּאַ֣ת שָׂדֶ֑ה וּמַעְשַׂ֥ר הַכֹּ֛ל לָרֹ֖ב הֵבִֽיאוּ׃
records.gloss: And as spread the word, multiplied [the] sons of Israel [the] first of grain, new wine and fresh oil and honey and all produce of [the] field; and [the] tithe of everything in abundance they brought.
pieces: As soon as the order went out, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} gave generously of the firstfruits of grain, new wine, oil, honey and all the produce of the fields. They brought in a great amount, a tithe of everything.

L.5: And as the word spread, the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel gave in abundance the first of grain, new wine and fresh oil and honey, and all the produce of the field; and the tithe of everything they brought in abundance.

R.5: As soon as the king's order spread, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} gave large amounts of the first part of their harvest: grain, new wine, olive oil, honey and everything that grew in their fields. They brought a tenth of everything, and it was a huge amount.

decisions.choice: the first of grain, new wine and oil: the firstfruits that belonged to the priests
decisions.reason: The first and best part of each harvest was given to Yahweh, and it went to the priests (Numbers 18:12-13; Deuteronomy 18:4).

decisions.choice: honey: perhaps syrup made from dates or other fruit, as well as bees' honey
decisions.reason: The word is used both of bees' honey (Judges 14:8) and of thick fruit syrup. Honey could be brought among the firstfruits, though it was not burned on the altar (Leviticus 2:11-12).

decisions.choice: the tithe of everything: the tenth that supported the Levites
decisions.reason: The law gave the tenth of the produce to the Levites in return for their service (Numbers 18:21-24; Leviticus 27:30).

decisions.choice: gave in abundance ... brought in abundance: the people gave far more than enough
decisions.reason: The verb "multiplied" and the phrase "in abundance" frame the verse, stressing how generously the people answered the king's order.

decisions.choice: the first part of their harvest; a tenth
decisions.reason: Readable explains "firstfruits" and "tithe" in common words.

decisions.choice: order
decisions.reason: The "word" that spread is the king's command of verse 4.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל וִֽיהוּדָ֗ה הַיּֽוֹשְׁבִים֮ בְּעָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָה֒ גַּם־הֵ֗ם מַעְשַׂ֤ר בָּקָר֙ וָצֹ֔אן וּמַעְשַׂ֣ר קָֽדָשִׁ֔ים הַמְקֻדָּשִׁ֖ים לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֑ם הֵבִ֕יאוּ וַֽיִּתְּנ֖וּ עֲרֵמ֥וֹת עֲרֵמֽוֹת׃ס
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Israel and Judah, the [ones] dwelling in [the] cities of Judah, also they [brought] a tithe of cattle and sheep, and a tithe of holy things, the [ones] consecrated to Yahweh their God, they brought; and they made heaps, heaps.
pieces: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and the people of Judah who lived in the towns of Judah also brought a tithe of cattle and sheep, and a tithe of the holy things that had been consecrated to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, and they piled them up in heap after heap.

L.6: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and Judah who lived in the cities of Judah, they also [brought] a tithe of cattle and sheep, and a tithe of holy things that were consecrated to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God they brought, and they laid [them in] heaps [upon] heaps.

R.6: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and the people of Judah who lived in the towns of Judah also brought a tenth of their cattle and sheep. They brought a tenth of the holy gifts set apart for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God as well. They piled it all up in great heaps.

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel and Judah who lived in Judah: northern Israelites settled in Judah, and the people of Judah
decisions.reason: Verse 5 spoke of the people of Jerusalem; now the people of the towns of Judah give too. "Sons of Israel" here most likely means people from the northern tribes who had come to live in Judah (11:16; 15:9; 30:25).

decisions.choice: a tithe of holy things consecrated to Yahweh: a tenth taken from gifts already set apart for Yahweh
alternatives: a tithe, being holy things consecrated to Yahweh
decisions.reason: The law speaks of a tithe of produce and of herds and flocks (Leviticus 27:30-32), but nowhere else of a tithe of holy things. The phrase may mean the gifts dedicated to Yahweh, of which a part went to the priests (Numbers 18:8-19), or the tithe itself, called holy because it belongs to Yahweh. The exact sense is not certain.

decisions.choice: heaps, heaps: heap after heap
decisions.reason: Saying the word twice shows a great number: one heap after another.

decisions.choice: the Israelites and the people of Judah
decisions.reason: "Sons of" covers both names in the Hebrew; Balanced and Readable add "the people of" before Judah.

records.source: בַּחֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֔י הֵחֵ֥לּוּ הָעֲרֵמ֖וֹת לְיִסּ֑וֹד וּבַחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֖י כִּלּֽוּ׃ס
records.gloss: In the month, the third, they began the heaps to found, and in the month, the seventh, they finished.
pieces: They began making the heaps in the third month and finished in the seventh month.

L.7: In the third month they began to found the heaps, and in the seventh month they finished.

R.7: They started making the piles in the third month of the year, and they finished in the seventh month.

decisions.choice: from the third month to the seventh: from the Festival of Weeks to the Festival of Booths
decisions.reason: The third month (about May to June) was the time of the wheat harvest and the Festival of Weeks (Exodus 34:22; Leviticus 23:15-21). The seventh month (about September to October) brought the end of the fruit and grape harvest and the Festival of Booths (Deuteronomy 16:13-15). The heaps grew through the whole harvest season, as each crop came in.

decisions.choice: to found the heaps: to lay the first layers of the heaps
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to lay a foundation. Here it is used for starting the piles.

decisions.choice: of the year
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the months are counted in the year.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ יְחִזְקִיָּ֣הוּ וְהַשָּׂרִ֔ים וַיִּרְא֖וּ אֶת־הָעֲרֵמ֑וֹת וַֽיְבָרֲכוּ֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה וְאֵ֖ת עַמּ֥וֹ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ
records.gloss: And came Hezekiah and the princes, and saw the heaps, and blessed Yahweh and his people Israel.
pieces: When Hezekiah and the officials came and looked at the heaps, they blessed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people Israel.

L.8: And Hezekiah and the princes came and saw the heaps, and they blessed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people Israel.

R.8: When Hezekiah and the leaders came and saw the piles, they praised {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to bless {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people Israel.

decisions.choice: blessed Yahweh and his people: praised Yahweh, and spoke blessing on the people
decisions.reason: One verb covers both. To bless Yahweh is to praise and thank him; to bless people is to speak good on them, asking Yahweh to show them favor (1 Chronicles 16:2).

decisions.choice: princes: the king's officials
decisions.reason: The word names the leading men of the kingdom who served under the king.

decisions.choice: praised the LORD and asked the LORD to bless
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the two senses of the one verb.

decisions.choice: princes (Literal); officials (Balanced); leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for this word in these books.

records.source: וַיִּדְרֹ֣שׁ יְחִזְקִיָּ֗הוּ עַל־הַכֹּֽהֲנִ֛ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֖ם עַל־הָעֲרֵמֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And inquired Hezekiah of the priests and the Levites about the heaps.
pieces: Hezekiah asked the priests and the Levites about the heaps.

L.9: And Hezekiah inquired of the priests and the Levites about the heaps.

R.9: Hezekiah asked the priests and the Levites about the piles.

decisions.choice: inquired: asked for an account
decisions.reason: The verb means to seek or ask carefully. Hezekiah wants to know why the heaps are still standing, and whether the priests and Levites are being supplied; Azariah's answer in verse 10 explains.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו עֲזַרְיָ֧הוּ הַכֹּהֵ֛ן הָרֹ֖אשׁ לְבֵ֣ית צָד֑וֹק וַ֠יֹּאמֶר מֵהָחֵ֨ל הַתְּרוּמָ֜ה לָבִ֣יא בֵית־יְהוָ֗ה אָכ֨וֹל וְשָׂב֤וֹעַ וְהוֹתֵר֙ עַד־לָר֔וֹב כִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ בֵּרַ֣ךְ אֶת־עַמּ֔וֹ וְהַנּוֹתָ֖ר אֶת־הֶהָמ֥וֹן הַזֶּֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And said to him Azariah the priest, the head, of [the] house of Zadok, and said, from beginning the contribution to bring [into the] house of Yahweh, eating and being satisfied and leaving over to abundance, for Yahweh has blessed his people; and the [thing] left over [is] this abundance.
pieces: Azariah the chief priest, of the family of Zadok, answered him, "Since the people began to bring the contributions into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, we have eaten our fill, with plenty left over, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people. This great amount is what is left."

L.10: And Azariah the priest, the chief, of the house of Zadok, said to him, and he said, "Since [they] began to bring the contribution into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, [we have been] eating and being satisfied and leaving over in abundance, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people; and what is left over [is] this great amount."

R.10: Azariah, the chief priest, who was from the family of Zadok, answered, "Ever since the people started bringing their gifts to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple, we have had all we could eat, and there has been a lot left over. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people. That is why so much is left."

decisions.choice: Azariah the chief priest, of the house of Zadok
decisions.reason: Zadok served as priest under David and became Solomon's chief priest (1 Kings 2:35); the chief priests after him came from his family (1 Chronicles 5:34-41, Hebrew numbering). This Azariah may or may not be the priest who stood up to Uzziah (26:17-20).

decisions.choice: the contribution: the gifts set apart for the sanctuary and its servants
decisions.reason: The word names what is lifted off and set apart from one's goods for Yahweh; in the law it covers the portions that went to the priests and Levites (Numbers 18:8-11, 24).

decisions.choice: eating, being satisfied and leaving over: the priests have had more than enough, again and again
decisions.reason: The three verbs are in a form that names the action without a person or time. The setting shows that the speaker means himself and his fellow priests and Levites, from the time the gifts began until now.

decisions.choice: eat and leave over: the language of Yahweh's supply
decisions.reason: The same pair of verbs is used when Yahweh feeds a hundred men with a small gift of bread: "they will eat and have some left over" (2 Kings 4:43-44).

decisions.choice: answered him
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "said to him ... and said" around the long name and title; Balanced and Readable say it once. Balanced and Readable also name "the people" as those who brought the gifts.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְחִזְקִיָּ֗הוּ לְהָכִ֧ין לְשָׁכ֛וֹת בְּבֵ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה וַיָּכִֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: And said Hezekiah to prepare chambers in [the] house of Yahweh, and they prepared [them].
pieces: Then Hezekiah gave orders to prepare storerooms in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they prepared them.

L.11: And Hezekiah said to prepare chambers in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they prepared [them].

R.11: Hezekiah ordered them to get storerooms ready in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple, and they did.

decisions.choice: chambers: rooms built around the temple courts, used for storing gifts and supplies
decisions.reason: The temple had side rooms around its courts where the priests and Levites kept the offerings, the tithes and the temple goods (1 Chronicles 9:26; 28:12; Nehemiah 13:4-5, 12).

decisions.choice: storerooms
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name what these rooms were for here; Literal keeps "chambers".

records.heading: Storerooms and their overseers

records.source: וַיָּבִ֨יאוּ אֶת־הַתְּרוּמָ֧ה וְהַֽמַּעֲשֵׂ֛ר וְהַקֳּדָשִׁ֖ים בֶּאֱמוּנָ֑ה וַעֲלֵיהֶ֤ם נָגִיד֙ כָּֽנַנְיָ֣הוּהַלֵּוִ֔י וְשִׁמְעִ֥י אָחִ֖יהוּ מִשְׁנֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And they brought the contribution and the tithe and the holy things in faithfulness; and over them [as] chief officer [was] Conaniah the Levite, and Shimei his brother [was] second.
pieces: They faithfully brought in the contributions, the tithes and the holy gifts. Conaniah the Levite was the chief officer over them, with his brother Shimei next in rank.

L.12: And they brought in the contribution and the tithe and the holy things faithfully; and over them [as] ruler [was] Conaniah the Levite, and Shimei his brother [was] second.

R.12: They were faithful in bringing in the gifts, the tenth parts and the holy gifts. Conaniah, a Levite, was in charge of all of it, and his brother Shimei was his assistant.

decisions.choice: in faithfulness: honestly and reliably
decisions.reason: The word means steadiness and trustworthiness. Those who brought in and stored the gifts could be relied on to handle them honestly; the word returns in verses 15 and 18.

decisions.choice: chief officer: the man in charge of the stores
decisions.reason: The word is often used of a ruler or prince, but in Chronicles it also names the officer at the head of a part of the temple's work (1 Chronicles 9:11, 20; 26:24).

decisions.choice: Conaniah: the name as the text is to be read
decisions.reason: The written letters of the name and the form marked in the margin for reading differ slightly; both give the same name, which appears again in verse 13.

decisions.choice: the gifts, the tenth parts
decisions.reason: Readable uses common words for "contributions" and "tithes".

decisions.choice: his assistant
decisions.reason: Readable says what "second" means: the next in charge, who helped Conaniah.

decisions.choice: ruler (Literal); chief officer (Balanced); in charge (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "ruler", the usual word for this title; Balanced and Readable say what the office was, as for the temple title in 1 Chronicles 9:11.

records.source: וִֽיחִיאֵ֡ל וַ֠עֲזַזְיָהוּ וְנַ֨חַת וַעֲשָׂהאֵ֜ל וִֽירִימ֤וֹת וְיוֹזָבָד֙ וֶאֱלִיאֵ֣ל וְיִסְמַכְיָ֔הוּ וּמַ֖חַת וּבְנָיָ֑הוּ פְּקִידִ֗ים מִיַּ֤ד כָּֽנַנְיָ֨הוּ֙ וְשִׁמְעִ֣י אָחִ֔יו בְּמִפְקַד֙ יְחִזְקִיָּ֣הוּ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַעֲזַרְיָ֖הוּ נְגִ֥יד בֵּית־הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: And Jehiel and Azaziah and Nahath and Asahel and Jerimoth and Jozabad and Eliel and Ismachiah and Mahath and Benaiah [were] overseers under [the] hand of Conaniah and Shimei his brother, by [the] appointment of Hezekiah the king and Azariah [the] chief officer of [the] house of God.
pieces: Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath and Benaiah were overseers under Conaniah and his brother Shimei, appointed by King Hezekiah and by Azariah the chief officer of the house of God.

L.13: And Jehiel and Azaziah and Nahath and Asahel and Jerimoth and Jozabad and Eliel and Ismachiah and Mahath and Benaiah [were] overseers under the hand of Conaniah and Shimei his brother, by the appointment of Hezekiah the king and Azariah the ruler of the house of God.

R.13: Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath and Benaiah were supervisors under Conaniah and his brother Shimei. King Hezekiah and Azariah, the official in charge of God's temple, had chosen them for this work.

decisions.choice: by the appointment of Hezekiah and Azariah: both the king and the chief priest appointed them
decisions.reason: The king and the chief priest act together in setting up the stores, as the king acts with the priests elsewhere in the reform (29:20-24). The phrase could also be read as naming Azariah as the officer over all of them, but the simplest reading joins him to the king in the appointing.

decisions.choice: chief officer of the house of God: the chief priest in his role of running the temple
decisions.reason: The same title is given to a chief priest in 1 Chronicles 9:11. Azariah is the chief priest of verse 10.

decisions.choice: under the hand of: working under the authority of
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for authority: the ten men answered to Conaniah and Shimei.

decisions.choice: supervisors
decisions.reason: Readable uses a common word for "overseers".

decisions.choice: the ruler of the house of God (Literal); the chief officer of the house of God (Balanced); the official in charge of God's temple (Readable)
decisions.reason: Worded as the same title in 1 Chronicles 9:11 and verse 12.

records.source: וְקוֹרֵ֨א בֶן־יִמְנָ֤ה הַלֵּוִי֙ הַשּׁוֹעֵ֣ר לַמִּזְרָ֔חָה עַ֖ל נִדְב֣וֹת הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים לָתֵת֙ תְּרוּמַ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה וְקָדְשֵׁ֖י הַקֳּדָשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: And Kore son of Imnah the Levite, the gatekeeper to the east, [was] over [the] freewill offerings of God, to give [the] contribution of Yahweh and [the] holy things of the holy things.
pieces: Kore son of Imnah the Levite, keeper of the East Gate, had charge of the freewill offerings made to God, to give out the contributions for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the most holy gifts.

L.14: And Kore son of Imnah the Levite, the gatekeeper at the east, [was] over the freewill offerings of God, to give out the contribution of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the holy things of the holy things.

R.14: Kore son of Imnah, a Levite who guarded the East Gate, was in charge of the gifts people chose to give to God. He gave out the gifts that had been given to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the most holy offerings.

decisions.choice: the gatekeeper at the east: keeper of the main gate of the temple
decisions.reason: The east gate faced the entrance of the temple, and its keepers held the chief post among the gatekeepers (1 Chronicles 9:18; 26:14, 17).

decisions.choice: freewill offerings: gifts given by choice, not because the law required them
decisions.reason: A freewill offering was given out of a willing heart, apart from any vow or duty (Leviticus 7:16; Deuteronomy 16:10).

decisions.choice: the holy things of the holy things: the most holy portions, which only the priests could eat
decisions.reason: Some parts of the offerings were called most holy: the grain offerings, sin offerings and guilt offerings, eaten only by the priests in a holy place (Leviticus 2:3; 6:10, 18; Numbers 18:9-10).

decisions.choice: to give: to hand out to those entitled to them
decisions.reason: Kore's task was to share out what came in among the priests and Levites.

decisions.choice: the most holy gifts (Balanced); the most holy offerings (Readable)
decisions.reason: The doubled phrase "holy of holies" means "most holy"; Literal keeps the Hebrew shape.

records.source: וְעַל־יָד֡וֹ עֵ֣דֶן וּ֠מִנְיָמִן וְיֵשׁ֨וּעַ וּֽשְׁמַֽעְיָ֜הוּ אֲמַרְיָ֧הוּ וּשְׁכַנְיָ֛הוּ בְּעָרֵ֥י הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים בֶּאֱמוּנָ֑ה לָתֵ֤ת לַאֲחֵיהֶם֙ בְּמַחְלְק֔וֹת כַּגָּד֖וֹל כַּקָּטָֽן׃
records.gloss: And under his hand [were] Eden and Miniamin and Jeshua and Shemaiah, Amariah and Shecaniah, in [the] cities of the priests, in faithfulness, to give to their brothers by divisions, as the great as the small,
pieces: Under him, in the towns of the priests, were Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah and Shecaniah, who faithfully gave out portions to their fellow priests and Levites by their divisions, to the great and the small alike,

L.15: And under his hand [were] Eden and Miniamin and Jeshua and Shemaiah, Amariah and Shecaniah, in the cities of the priests, in faithfulness, to give to their brothers by divisions, the great as the small,

R.15: Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah and Shecaniah helped him in the towns where the priests lived. They could be trusted to give out shares to their relatives by their groups, to everyone alike, from the greatest to the least.

decisions.choice: the cities of the priests: the towns given to the priests to live in
decisions.reason: Thirteen towns in Judah and Benjamin were given to the priests (Joshua 21:9-19; 1 Chronicles 6:39-45, Hebrew numbering). Many priests and Levites lived there when they were not on duty at the temple, so the portions had to reach them at home.

decisions.choice: the great as the small: everyone alike
decisions.reason: The pair covers everyone, whether important or not, older or younger; no one was passed over.

decisions.choice: their brothers: their fellow priests and Levites
decisions.reason: "Brothers" is used for members of the same tribe or the same service, not only for sons of one father.

decisions.choice: gave out portions to their fellow priests and Levites
decisions.reason: Balanced supplies "portions" as the object of the giving, and says who "their brothers" were.

decisions.choice: the record ends with a comma
decisions.reason: The sentence continues into verse 16, which says who was or was not included; Literal and Balanced end this record with a comma. Readable makes each verse a sentence of its own.

records.source: מִלְּבַ֞ד הִתְיַחְשָׂ֣ם לִזְכָרִ֗ים מִבֶּ֨ן שָׁל֤וֹשׁ שָׁנִים֙ וּלְמַ֔עְלָה לְכָל־הַבָּ֥א לְבֵית־יְהוָ֖ה לִדְבַר־י֣וֹם בְּיוֹמ֑וֹ לַעֲב֣וֹדָתָ֔ם בְּמִשְׁמְרוֹתָ֖ם כְּמַחְלְקוֹתֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: apart from their being enrolled, to males from a son of three years and upward, to everyone coming to [the] house of Yahweh for [the] matter of a day in its day, for their service in their duties according to their divisions.
pieces: apart from the males three years old and up who were enrolled in the genealogies, all who came into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to do the work each day required, serving in their duties by their divisions.

L.16: apart from their enrollment by genealogy, of males from three years old and upward, everyone who came into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for the duty of each day in its day, for their service in their duties according to their divisions.

R.16: This was apart from the males three years old and older who were listed in the family records, who went into {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple to do each day's work, serving in their duties by their groups.

decisions.choice: apart from: the portions in the towns did not include the men on duty at the temple
decisions.reason: The word usually means "besides" or "apart from". The likely sense is that the men who came to the temple for their turn of service were fed there from the offerings, so the officers in the towns gave to everyone else. It could also mean "in addition to", so that both groups received portions.

decisions.choice: three years old: as the text stands
decisions.reason: Boys of three would hardly come into the temple to serve. The text may mean that the males were enrolled from that age and fed with their fathers, or the number may once have been "thirty", which differs by a small change in Hebrew and is the age at which Levites began full service in Numbers 4:3. The text as it stands says three, and that is kept.

decisions.choice: the matter of a day in its day: the work required on each day
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of a daily share or duty, set for each day as it comes (Exodus 5:13; 1 Chronicles 16:37).

decisions.choice: This was apart from
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence and supplies "This was" to connect it to verse 15.

records.source: וְאֵ֨ת הִתְיַחֵ֤שׂ הַכֹּהֲנִים֙ לְבֵ֣ית אֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֔ם וְהַ֨לְוִיִּ֔ם מִבֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וּלְמָ֑עְלָה בְּמִשְׁמְרוֹתֵיהֶ֖ם בְּמַחְלְקוֹתֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And the enrollment of the priests by [the] house of their fathers, and the Levites from a son of twenty years and upward, in their duties by their divisions;
pieces: The priests were enrolled by their ancestral families, and the Levites from twenty years old and up by their duties and their divisions,

L.17: And the enrollment of the priests [was] by the house of their fathers, and the Levites from twenty years old and upward, in their duties by their divisions;

R.17: The priests were listed by their families. The Levites twenty years old and older were listed by their duties and their groups.

decisions.choice: the enrollment of the priests: the list by which portions were given
alternatives: and they gave to the enrolled priests
decisions.reason: The verse begins with the word that marks an object, as if it continues the giving of verse 15: the officers gave to those on the priests' list and the Levites' list. It may also simply state how the lists were kept. The sense is the same: the lists decided who received a portion.

decisions.choice: the Levites from twenty years old: as David had ordered
decisions.reason: David lowered the age at which Levites began serving to twenty (1 Chronicles 23:24, 27).

decisions.choice: house of their fathers (Literal); ancestral families (Balanced); families (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for this phrase in these books.

records.source: וּלְהִתְיַחֵ֗שׂ בְּכָל־טַפָּ֧ם נְשֵׁיהֶ֛ם וּבְנֵיהֶ֥ם וּבְנוֹתֵיהֶ֖ם לְכָל־קָהָ֑ל כִּ֥י בֶאֱמוּנָתָ֖ם יִתְקַדְּשׁוּ־קֹֽדֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: and to enroll with all their little ones, their wives and their sons and their daughters, to all [the] assembly; for in their faithfulness they consecrated themselves [in] holiness.
pieces: and to all who were enrolled with them: their little children, their wives, their sons and their daughters, the whole company. For they had been faithful in keeping themselves holy.

L.18: and to the enrolled with all their little ones, their wives and their sons and their daughters, for all the assembly; for in their faithfulness they consecrated themselves [in] holiness.

R.18: The shares also went to everyone listed with them: their little children, wives, sons and daughters, the whole group. For the priests and Levites had been faithful in keeping themselves holy.

decisions.choice: and to the enrolled: the portions also went to the families on the lists
decisions.reason: The verse continues the giving of verse 15: the whole households of the priests and Levites, children included, received a share.

decisions.choice: in their faithfulness they consecrated themselves: they kept themselves holy and faithful in their service
decisions.reason: The word for faithfulness can also mean a position of trust (1 Chronicles 9:22, 26). Then the sense would be that in their office of trust they kept themselves holy. Either way the reason given is the priests' and Levites' faithful, holy service, which is why their families were provided for.

decisions.choice: to all the assembly: the whole company of priests and Levites with their families
decisions.reason: "Assembly" here is the whole group on the lists, not the gathering of all Israel.

decisions.choice: The shares also went to ... the priests and Levites
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence and names who received and who had kept themselves holy.

records.source: וְלִבְנֵי֩ אַהֲרֹ֨ן הַכֹּהֲנִ֜ים בִּשְׂדֵ֨י מִגְרַ֤שׁ עָרֵיהֶם֙ בְּכָל־עִ֣יר וָעִ֔יר אֲנָשִׁ֕ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִקְּב֖וּ בְּשֵׁמ֑וֹת לָתֵ֣ת מָנ֗וֹת לְכָל־זָכָר֙ בַּכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים וּלְכָל־הִתְיַחֵ֖שׂ בַּלְוִיִּֽם׃
records.gloss: And for [the] sons of Aaron, the priests, in [the] fields of [the] pastureland of their cities, in every city and city, [there were] men who were designated by names to give portions to every male among the priests and to every [one] enrolled among the Levites.
pieces: For the descendants of Aaron, the priests, who lived in the pasturelands around their towns, there were men in every town who were named to give portions to every male among the priests and to everyone enrolled among the Levites.

L.19: And for the sons of Aaron, the priests, in the fields of the pastureland of their cities, in each and every city, [there were] men who were designated by name to give portions to every male among the priests and to everyone enrolled among the Levites.

R.19: Aaron's descendants, the priests, also lived on the farmland around their towns. In every town, men were chosen by name to give shares to every male priest and to every Levite who was listed in the family records.

decisions.choice: the fields of the pastureland: the open land around the priests' towns
decisions.reason: Each town given to the priests and Levites had land around it for their herds and flocks (Numbers 35:2-5; Leviticus 25:34). Those who lived out there were also reached.

decisions.choice: every city and city: each and every town
decisions.reason: Repeating the noun means "every single one".

decisions.choice: designated by names: chosen and listed by name
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used of men named for a task (1 Chronicles 12:32; 16:41; 2 Chronicles 28:15).

decisions.choice: Aaron's descendants ... also lived on the farmland around their towns. In every town ...
decisions.reason: Readable splits the verse into two sentences and says "farmland" for the pastureland.

records.source: וַיַּ֧עַשׂ כָּזֹ֛את יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ בְּכָל־יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיַּ֨עַשׂ הַטּ֤וֹב וְהַיָּשָׁר֙ וְהָ֣אֱמֶ֔ת לִפְנֵ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And did like this Hezekiah in all Judah, and he did the good and the right and the faithfulness before Yahweh his God.
pieces: Hezekiah did this throughout Judah. He did what was good and right and faithful before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God.

L.20: And Hezekiah did like this in all Judah, and he did what was good and what was right and what was faithful before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God.

R.20: Hezekiah did this all through Judah. He did what was good, right and faithful in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God.

decisions.choice: faithful: true and reliable
decisions.reason: The word means truth, firmness and faithfulness. Here it describes the king's conduct: loyal and true to Yahweh. In Kings, Hezekiah prays that he has walked before Yahweh "in faithfulness" with a whole heart (2 Kings 20:3).

decisions.choice: good and right before Yahweh: the verdict on Hezekiah, made fuller
decisions.reason: Chronicles has already said that Hezekiah did what was right in Yahweh's sight (29:2; 2 Kings 18:3). Here it adds "good" and "faithful", and says "before" Yahweh rather than "in his eyes": the king lived his life in Yahweh's presence.

decisions.choice: in the presence of
decisions.reason: Readable makes "before" clear: in the sight of Yahweh.

records.source: וּבְכָֽל־מַעֲשֶׂ֞ה אֲשֶׁר־הֵחֵ֣ל׀בַּעֲבוֹדַ֣ת בֵּית־הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים וּבַתּוֹרָה֙ וּבַמִּצְוָ֔ה לִדְרֹ֖שׁ לֵֽאלֹהָ֑יו בְּכָל־לְבָב֥וֹ עָשָׂ֖ה וְהִצְלִֽיחַ׃פ
records.gloss: And in every work that he began in [the] service of [the] house of God, and in the law and in the commandment, to seek his God, with all his heart he did, and prospered.
pieces: Every work he took up in the service of the house of God, and in keeping the law and the commandments, he did with all his heart, seeking his God; and he prospered.

L.21: And in every work that he began in the service of the house of God, and in the law and in the commandment, to seek his God, with all his heart he did [it], and he prospered.

R.21: He served God's temple and obeyed God's law and commands in everything he started, because he wanted to seek his God. He put his whole heart into it, and he was successful.

decisions.choice: to seek his God: to turn to God, worship him and obey him
decisions.reason: Seeking God is a key thought in Chronicles: those who seek him find him and are blessed, and those who forsake him are forsaken (1 Chronicles 28:9; 2 Chronicles 15:2; 26:5). Hezekiah's work for the temple and the law is described as seeking God.

decisions.choice: he prospered: success follows faithfulness
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 18:7 says the same of Hezekiah: Yahweh was with him and he prospered. Chronicles links the success to his seeking God with all his heart, as it does with Uzziah (26:5) and with the words of Jehoshaphat (20:20).

decisions.choice: with all his heart: with his whole will and devotion
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought and will. To act with all one's heart is to hold nothing back (Deuteronomy 6:5; 2 Chronicles 15:15).

decisions.choice: in keeping the law and the commandments
decisions.reason: Balanced supplies "keeping" to show how the law and commandment belong in the list of his works.

decisions.choice: obeyed God's law and commands; because he wanted to seek his God
decisions.reason: Readable supplies "obeyed", names whose law it is, and turns "to seek his God" into the reason for his work.
